questions.text: Why is proper hand washing important for food handlers?
questions.explanation: Proper hand washing removes harmful microorganisms and reduces the risk of contaminating food.

answers.text: It removes harmful microorganisms from the hands.
It makes gloves unnecessary in every situation.
It keeps food warmer during preparation.
It replaces the need to clean work surfaces.

questions.text: When should a food handler wash their hands?
questions.explanation: Hands should be washed before handling food and after activities that may contaminate them, such as handling raw food, using the toilet, touching waste, coughing or sneezing.

answers.text: Only at the beginning of the working day.
Before handling food and after any activity that may contaminate the hands.
Only when the hands look dirty.

questions.text: What is cross-contamination?
questions.explanation: Cross-contamination is the transfer of harmful microorganisms or allergens from one food, person, utensil or surface to another.

answers.text: The transfer of harmful microorganisms or allergens from one source to another.
Cooking food at a high temperature.

questions.text: Which practice best helps prevent cross-contamination?
questions.explanation: Raw food should be kept separate from ready-to-eat food, and separate clean equipment should be used where appropriate.

answers.text: Use the same chopping board for raw chicken and salad without cleaning it.
Store raw meat above ready-to-eat food.
Keep raw food separate from ready-to-eat food and use clean equipment.
Wash raw chicken in the sink before cooking.

questions.text: Where should raw meat normally be stored in a refrigerator?
questions.explanation: Raw meat should be covered and stored below ready-to-eat food so that drips cannot contaminate other foods.

answers.text: On the top shelf above cooked food.
Covered, on a lower shelf below ready-to-eat food.
Inside an open container beside desserts.

questions.text: What is the recommended refrigerator temperature range for chilled food?
questions.explanation: Refrigerated food should generally be kept between 0°C and 5°C.

questions.text: What core temperature should food normally reach when cooked thoroughly?
questions.explanation: Food should reach a core temperature of at least 75°C instantaneously, or an equivalent time-and-temperature combination.

questions.text: Where should the temperature of cooked food be checked?
questions.explanation: The temperature should be checked at the core or thickest part of the food.

answers.text: At the core or thickest part.
On the plate beside the food.

questions.text: What is the minimum temperature commonly used for hot holding?
questions.explanation: Hot-held food should generally be maintained at 63°C or above.

questions.text: What temperature should reheated food normally reach at its core?
questions.explanation: Reheated food should be piping hot and reach at least 70°C at the core.

questions.text: How many times should previously cooked food normally be reheated?
questions.explanation: Food should normally be reheated only once to reduce food safety risks.

answers.text: It should never be reheated under any circumstances.

questions.text: What should a food handler do if they have vomiting or diarrhoea?
questions.explanation: A food handler with vomiting or diarrhoea should report it to their manager and must not handle food while they may pose a contamination risk.

answers.text: Continue working but wear two pairs of gloves.
Report the illness and do not handle food.
Take a short break and return immediately.

questions.text: What should be done with a cut on a food handler's hand?
questions.explanation: Cuts should be cleaned and completely covered with a suitable waterproof, highly visible dressing.

answers.text: Leave it uncovered so it can dry.
Cover it with a suitable waterproof, highly visible dressing.
Cover it with a piece of paper towel.
Dip it in sanitiser before every task.

questions.text: Which statement about disposable gloves is correct?
questions.explanation: Gloves do not replace hand washing and must be changed when contaminated or when moving between incompatible tasks.

answers.text: Gloves replace the need to wash hands.
One pair of gloves can be worn for an entire shift.
Gloves must be washed and reused.
Gloves do not replace hand washing and must be changed when necessary.

questions.text: What is the safest way to defrost frozen food?
questions.explanation: Food should be defrosted under controlled conditions, such as in a refrigerator, so that it does not remain at unsafe temperatures.

answers.text: In a refrigerator or another approved controlled method.

questions.text: What does HACCP help a food business do?
questions.explanation: HACCP helps a food business identify, evaluate and control hazards that may affect food safety.

answers.text: Identify and control food safety hazards.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a physical food hazard?
questions.explanation: A physical hazard is a foreign object in food, such as broken glass, metal fragments or stones.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a chemical food hazard?
questions.explanation: Cleaning chemicals, pesticides and other chemical residues can contaminate food and create a chemical hazard.

questions.text: How many specified food allergens must be declared under EU food information rules?
questions.explanation: There are 14 specified allergens that must be declared when used as ingredients.

questions.text: What is the correct response when a customer asks about allergens in a dish?
questions.explanation: Staff should use accurate, up-to-date allergen information and should never guess.

answers.text: Guess based on how the dish looks.
Provide accurate, up-to-date information and never guess.
Tell the customer that small amounts never matter.
Ask the customer to taste a small amount first.
